verses.1: And Jehovah sent Nathan to David. He came to him and said, “There were two men in one city: one was rich, and the other was poor.”
verses.2: The rich man had a lot of sheep and cattle.
verses.3: And the lamb was nothing more than a small little animal. It was purchased, and it lived along with its owner. Together with its children, it ate from its mother’s breast, drank from its mother’s teats, and slept in its mother’s arms. It became like a beloved child to its owner.
verses.4: And he went to a rich man and asked for money from him, as well as food for the guest who came to visit him. He took the man’s coat and made it into clothes for the guest who came to him.
verses.5: And David cut off the ear of that man. Then he said to Nathan, “May the LORD live! This man is the son of death.”
verses.6: And the price for this will be four times as much, because he has done this deed, and because he did not fear God.
verses.7: And Nathan said to David, “You are the man whom Jehovah, the God of Israel, has chosen to be king over Israel. I will make you king over Israel, and I will save you from Saul’s hands.”
verses.8: And I will give you your house and your wives as well. I will also give you the houses of Israel and Judah. And if there’s any surplus, I will give it to you as a gift.
verses.9: Why did you do what the LORD commanded you to do? You did evil in His eyes. You took Uria’s wife from him, and you killed him in battle. You took his wife as your own.
verses.10: And now, do not allow any destruction to come from your house forever. For in that situation, you took away my beloved Uria, who was meant to be your wife.
verses.11: So said Jehovah: “I will bring calamity upon you from your homes. I will take your women and give them to your enemies. They will lie with your women before the sun rises.”
verses.12: For you did it in secret, but I will do this thing against all of Israel and against the sun.
verses.13: And David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against God.” Nathan replied, “Nathan says to David, ‘May God take away your sin.’”
verses.14: May you be cursed, for you have offended the LORD with these words. Even the child will die because of your actions.
verses.15: And Nathan went to his house. Then Jehovah rejected the child that Esau’s wife had given birth to for David.
verses.16: David asked God for help for the young man. David sacrificed an animal, and then he went to Lana. He lay down on the ground.
verses.17: And the elders of his house stood up to raise him from the ground. But he did not create them as bread.
verses.18: On the seventh day, the child died. David’s servants saw that the child was dead. They said to him, “Look, the child is dead! When he was still alive, we spoke to him, but he didn’t listen to us. How can we say to him, ‘The child is dead’?” And they did something bad.
verses.19: David saw that his servants were being harmed. David mourned for the dead child. He said to his servants, “The child is dead.” They replied, “Yes, it’s dead.”
verses.20: David got up from the ground, washed himself, and changed his clothes. Then he went into the Temple of God. He bowed down, and went into his house. There, he asked for food to eat. They gave him bread to eat.
verses.21: And his servants said to him, “What is this that you have done regarding the child? When the child was alive, you mourned and fasted; but when the child died, you ate bread again.”
verses.22: And as the child was still alive, he said, “May I live and die, for I have said that no one knows. May Jehovah bless me, and may the child live.”
verses.23: And now, why must I suffer this? I can’t get him back anymore. I go to him, but he doesn’t return to me.
verses.24: David comforted his daughter, Sheba. He went to her and lay with her. She gave birth to a son. They named him Solomon. And God loved him.
verses.25: And he sent it through Nathan the prophet’s hand. He called out his name, Yidiyyah, in the name of Jehovah.
verses.26: Yoav fought against the people of Amnon. He captured the city that was ruled by them.
verses.27: And Joshua sent messengers to David, and he said, “I will fight against the king, and I will destroy his city.”
verses.28: And now, I will gather the rest of the people together. I will lay siege to the city, so that I may take it by force. Then its name will be given to me.
verses.29: David gathered all the people together. Then he went out and fought against them. And he defeated them.
verses.30: And he took the crown of their king from on his head. Its weight was equal to that of gold and precious stones. The crown was placed on David’s head, and the treasures of the city were also brought out in great quantities.
verses.31: And he brought out the people who were in those cities, and he placed them in the camps and in the bars of iron. He also moved them to other places. He did the same with all the cities of the people of Israel. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
